producer_report.summary: The checks stage now reads GitHub's CI result for the candidate. No email-like text is written anywhere. `Athena::with_ci_source` in `run/mod.rs` replaces the unconditional `routing::NoCi` and picks the CI source and the wait together. A nested run, or an origin that is not an https URL on github.com (none, a local path, another host, an ssh remote), gets `NoCi` with one read and no sleep. A GitHub origin gets a `gh::GhClient` over `gh::GhCli`, which reads the push run on `athena/ci/<job id>` for the candidate SHA. It reads once, then every 20 s up to the new `[budget] ci_wait_s`: default 1500, set explicitly in `athena.toml`, 76 reads and 75 sleeps. `routing.rs` gains `CI_POLL`, `ci_polls`, a `Paced` wrapper that sleeps through an injected sleeper, and `run_routed_with_record`, which also returns the CI record. `ci_result.rs` is untouched. Green skips the local checks and each check note names the CI run. Red fails with the failing check named and no local run. A missing, cancelled, timed-out or unfinished run falls back to the local checks. When the checks came from CI, `verify::reuse_statement` for the candidate reaches the verifier as a `ci-result` entry that is not a check; a resumed job carries none. The userinfo split in `GhClient::origin_repository` uses `'\u{40}'` with a comment saying why. The test credential URL is built from pieces. A scan of the added lines found no at-sign. Root cause of the earlier fault: a literal at-sign form in `gh/client.rs`.

checks_run.note: 5 new tests: green, red, fallbacks (missing, unfinished, cancelled, timed out), no-origin forms, verifier statement.
769 passed in athena-core, 140 in athena-data, 0 failed. This includes the config load tests, the routing unit tests, the existing GitHub-origin tests and refusal_corpus.
It ran once, but the output was too large to read in this environment, so I have no result. I reran only the two changed crates, above. Athena's recorded run decides the rest.

The recording check_seam executor list is empty, one runs read was made, and no sleep happened. Every recorded check note contains 'CI run <address> for <candidate sha>'. The job lands.

A green reply was ready, so a wrong CI read would have skipped them. routing::tests::routing_no_wait_is_one_read_and_no_pause covers NoCi and a bound of 0, with one read and no sleep.

open_issues: A failed or skipped push of the CI branch only warns (push_ci_branch in gh/early.rs returns nothing), so with a GitHub origin the wait still runs to the bound (up to 1500 s) before the local checks start. Follow-up for a job that may edit gh/early.rs: report whether the candidate is on the branch, so with_ci_source can choose NoCi when it is not. Until then, lower ci_wait_s to shorten the cost.
GhClient::origin_repository duplicates the private https_github_repository in gh/early.rs, so the two could drift. Follow-up: have early.rs delegate to it.

Departure from the plan: instead of a separate CiSteps capability, the test capability Docs got an ci_steps flag, off by default, so existing tests are unchanged. The helper swaps in the three-check variant. The same applies to the CiSteps capability's role in the plan (fmt, clippy, test, no path skip).
Departure from the plan: the origin check is the associated function GhClient::origin_repository, not a free pub(crate) function. GhClient is already exported, so gh/mod.rs stays unchanged.
No test drives a real resumed job to show it carries no reuse statement. That holds by construction, because the recorded_checks branch never sets the statement. The CHANGELOG states it.
I could not read the output of the one whole-workspace cargo test run (saved outside the working directory), so that run's result is unknown.
mistakes: My first full cargo test --locked output was too large to read in this environment, and I could not open the saved file. I reran the two changed crates with --quiet instead of the whole workspace.
learnings: gh/client.rs is a private module of gh. Only the types re-exported in gh/mod.rs (GhClient, GhCli, Runner, ci_branch, parse_ci_run) are reachable from run/mod.rs, so an associated function on GhClient avoids touching gh/mod.rs.
ci_result::read_ci sleeps itself with std::thread::sleep(wait.pause). A Paced CiSource wrapper plus a Wait with pause ZERO gives an observable 20 s step with no real sleeping.
A finished run whose aggregate job is cancelled or timed out is Missing at once in read_ci, so it is not waited for. Only an absent or unfinished run waits the whole bound.
Baseline checks go through run_check, not check_seam, so only the candidate checks are counted by the recording executor.
The capability id 'study' routes as kind Study, so route.reuse is on whenever the capability's checks cover fmt, clippy and test.
desires: A way to see the tail of a long cargo test run, such as a quiet or summary mode in the allowed commands.
